Name: SQL Injection
Description: Untrusted user input is directly concatenated into SQL query strings allowing attackers to bypass authentication or extract arbitrary database records.

Name: OS Command Injection
Description: Untrusted input is passed directly to system shell execution primitives (e.g., system or exec) allowing arbitrary server-side operating system commands.

Name: Command Injection (General)
Description: Improper neutralization of special characters when constructing operating system commands across process boundaries.

Name: Code Injection (Eval / Dynamic Execution)
Description: Untrusted data is passed to dynamic code evaluation interpreters (e.g., eval or Function constructor) executing arbitrary code within the host application.

Name: Eval Injection
Description: Specific variant of code injection where user input is executed directly inside dynamic language eval constructs.

Name: Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI)
Description: Untrusted input is parsed directly as a server template string (e.g., Jinja2 or EJS) enabling remote code execution via template reflection.

Name: NoSQL Injection
Description: Untrusted input containing MongoDB or CouchDB query selectors ($gt or $where) is processed without type sanitization altering query semantics.

Name: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
Description: Untrusted input is reflected in HTML responses or DOM manipulation sinks without context-aware escaping executing scripts in user browsers.

Name: Direct & Indirect Prompt Injection
Description: Adversarial user input overrides system instructions in LLM agent pipelines or untrusted retrieved RAG data hijacks model behavior.

Name: Improper Output Handling (LLM Execution Sinks)
Description: Raw completions generated by LLMs are piped directly to sensitive downstream execution sinks (SQL, OS shell, DOM) without schema validation.

Name: Path Traversal / Arbitrary File Inclusion
Description: Untrusted file path parameters containing dot-dot-slash (../) sequences allow reading or writing files outside the intended root directory.

Name: Open Redirect
Description: Untrusted URL input in redirection routines allows attackers to redirect users to external phishing or malicious websites.

Name: Missing Authorization Decorator / Route Guard
Description: Sensitive administrative or privileged web routes lack explicit authentication/authorization decorators or middleware verifications.

Name: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF)
Description: State-changing HTTP endpoints lack anti-forgery validation tokens allowing unauthorized commands transmitted from trusted web users.

Name: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
Description: Server-side network fetch routines fetch attacker-supplied URLs without restricting loopback or internal cloud metadata addresses.

Name: Sensitive Information Disclosure in Context
Description: Environment secrets, API tokens, or private user data are inadvertently included in LLM context windows or logs.

Name: System Prompt & Intellectual Property Leakage
Description: Prompt extraction techniques or unprotected system endpoints reveal proprietary system prompts and guardrails.

Name: Insecure Deserialization
Description: Untrusted serialized byte streams (e.g., Python pickle or node-serialize) are reconstituted into memory executing arbitrary payload code.

Name: Prototype Pollution
Description: Recursive merging of user-supplied objects in JavaScript modifies Object.prototype leading to property injection or denial of service.

Name: Mass Assignment / Object Attribute Overwrite
Description: HTTP parameters are bound directly to internal data models or database entity constructors allowing modification of privileged fields.

Name: Use of Hard-coded Credentials
Description: Plaintext API keys, database passwords, or encryption tokens are hardcoded into source code repository files.

Name: Broken or Risky Cryptographic Algorithm
Description: Use of cryptographically broken symmetric ciphers (e.g., DES, RC4, Blowfish) or insecure block cipher modes (e.g., ECB mode).

Name: Use of Weak Hash Algorithm
Description: Use of cryptographically broken or collision-prone hash functions (e.g., MD5, SHA-1) for password storage or sensitive integrity verification.

Name: Use of Weak PRNG for Security Tokens
Description: Use of non-cryptographic random number generators (e.g., Python random or Math.random) for session tokens or password reset keys.

Name: JWT Signature Verification Bypass
Description: JSON Web Token decode functions configured with verify_signature=False or algorithms accepting 'none' bypass token integrity.

Name: XML External Entity (XXE) Injection
Description: XML parsers configured with external entity resolution or DTD processing enabled read internal files or initiate outbound SSRF.

Name: Regular Expression Denial of Service (ReDoS)
Description: Vulnerable regular expressions with nested quantifiers cause exponential catastrophic backtracking when processing crafted inputs.

Name: Debug Mode Active / Verbose Error Stack Exposure
Description: Web framework debug flags (DEBUG=True) or unhandled exception handlers expose sensitive stack traces and server variables.
